title: Harmony Museum

services.name: Facility Rentals
services.desc: The Harmony Museum offers three unique venues that will enhance your event or celebration. There’s a modern hall with access to a commercial kitchen for you or the caterer of your choice. It also has access to an 1809 wine cellar-very cool! There’s an amazing, rustic barn-one of the oldest west of the Allegheny Mountains. And there’s smaller, reverent space that once was a Mennonite Meetinghouse-now on the national register of historic places. One museum-three great venues. services.name: Walking Tour
services.desc: The walking tour of Historic Harmony will allow you to browse through our quaint community to see buildings built by the Harmonists in the early 1800’s, walk-through both the Harmonists and Mennonite cemeteries, and even grab a cup of coffee or a bite to eat. The hike can be as long or as short as you desire. If you want to do the entire hike, plan on at least 2 hours and about 3 miles of walking, but you can see most of the properties within the town in 20 minutes and just ¼ mile of flat walking. services.name: Weavers Cabin
services.desc: Big news: the Harmony Museum’s Weavers Cabin in now rented by the volunteers. This will allow them to sell their goods, as well as continuing to demonstrate and educate visitors. This reconstructed two-story cabin houses the Harmony Museum Weavers. This talented group works on antique and reproduction looms to replicate the goods that the Harmonists produced for sale here. Quality woolen and linen fabrics and even silk came from the looms that were employed by the enterprising Harmonists. Several days a week the Museum Weavers demonstrate this art to visitors and sell their wares.
